title: How to plan a month with three paydays when you're paid every two weeks
seoTitle: How to plan a month with three paydays
description: If you're paid every two weeks, most years have two months with three paydays. Find yours for 2027 in one table, and see how they line up with your bills.
howWeChecked: Written by the flourish team, with AI tools used to help draft it. The payday table is our own calendar count for 2027. The payroll and budgeting facts were read on November 12, 2026 on the Government of Canada pages linked in the text. No financial professional reviewed this page.

sources.label: Canada Revenue Agency, Payroll Deductions Formulas (T4127), 122nd edition
Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, Making a budget
Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, Budget Planner

body.html: If your employer pays you every two weeks, you usually have 26 paydays a year, rather than 24. Most months have two paydays, and usually two months have three. Some years have 27 paydays. This guide shows where the third one comes from, which months it lands in for 2027, and what a calendar can show you about it.

body.text: Where the third payday comes from

body.html: A year has 52 weeks and one day (two in a leap year). Every two weeks works out to 26 paydays. Twelve months with two paydays each is only 24. The other two have to go somewhere, so two months get a third.

The Canada Revenue Agency's payroll formulas say the same thing from the employer's side: a biweekly year can have 26 or 27 pay periods, and employers are told to work out the number at the start of the year (CRA, Payroll Deductions Formulas, 122nd edition, effective January 1, 2026, last checked November 12, 2026). In 2027, a first payday on January 1 gives you 27 paydays. The other starting dates in the table give you 26.
Look up the date of your first payday in January 2027. If you don't know it yet, count forward 14 days at a time from your last payday.

How this table was made: we counted forward 14 days at a time from each start date through December 31, 2027 and counted the paydays in each month. It is calendar arithmetic, with no estimate in it. It assumes your payday stays exactly 14 days apart. Some employers move a payday that lands on a holiday or a weekend, so check your own pay schedule.
For the rest of 2026: December 2026 has three paydays only if your first December payday is the 1st, 2nd or 3rd.

body.text: Why the month still feels tight

body.html: A third payday doesn't arrive on top of the month. It arrives at the edge of it. In a three-payday month, the first payday is in the first few days and the third is in the last few days. Bills often have fixed monthly due dates, while biweekly paydays fall on different dates each month. The gap between a payday and a bill can change.
That changing gap is the thing to watch. The stretch between a payday and the bills due before the next one can change from month to month, even when your pay and your bills are the same size.

body.text: What a three-payday calendar can show

body.html: The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada describes a budget as a plan for managing your money, and suggests comparing your budget to what you actually spend at the end of each month (FCAC, Making a budget, last checked November 12, 2026).

A calendar with paydays, bill due dates and benefit payment dates shows how income and expenses line up. Government benefit dates move too. The Canada child benefit, for example, is issued on December 11, 2026 and then on January 20, 2027 (Benefits payment dates, canada.ca, last checked November 12, 2026).

Bills can be grouped by the last payday before their due date. In a three-payday month, bills can fall between three paydays. Some bills may also be due before the month's first payday. In some three-payday months, one group has fewer bills than the others. That is the "extra" paycheque people talk about. It isn't extra pay. It is the same pay with fewer bills attached to it.

FCAC's budgeting page lists goals people commonly set, such as paying off a credit card, starting an emergency fund or paying down debts. It suggests an emergency fund of 3 to 6 months of living expenses, built by putting a small amount away regularly. Which goal fits is your call.
FCAC also has a Budget Planner that lets you enter income and expenses and store your budget online (last checked November 12, 2026).
flourish is built around paydays instead of calendar months, so a three-payday month needs no special setup.
